# Rounak Neema

> Security-Oriented Software Engineer | DevSecOps | Systems & Infrastructure

Rounak Neema is a Computer Science engineer focused on cybersecurity, high-performance networking, backend systems, DevSecOps, cloud infrastructure, and AI-powered developer tooling.

Primary technical areas include Go, Python, Linux, networking, vulnerability assessment, distributed systems, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, CI/CD, microservices, security analytics, LLM applications, and AI agents.

## Projects

### Revealr

[Project](https://revealr.rounakneema.in)

High-concurrency adaptive network scanner and vulnerability-mapping platform built with Go and Python.

Key areas:
- Concurrent network and port scanning
- Service and version fingerprinting
- Offline vulnerability mapping
- Stateful SQLite-backed scan management
- Historical baseline comparison
- Network drift detection
- Modular Python security plugins
- Protocol analysis and custom vulnerability checks
- IDS/IPS-aware scanning profiles

A documented benchmark reports approximately 50,000 ports/minute under the tested configuration.

Technologies: Go, Python, SQLite, networking, concurrency, vulnerability assessment.

### MetroMind

[Project](https://metromind.rounakneema.in)

Enterprise AI document-intelligence platform developed for the Smart India Hackathon and designed around Kochi Metro Rail document workflows.

Key areas:
- Microservices architecture
- Document processing
- OCR and search workflows
- Multi-tenant architecture
- RBAC
- Authentication and authorization
- Audit logging
- Docker and Docker Compose
- Backend APIs and data pipelines

Technologies: Go, Docker, REST APIs, microservices, SQL, RBAC, audit logging, AI/document intelligence.

### OSA — Offline Security Auditor

[Project](https://osa.rounakneema.in)

Offline-first security analytics and threat-detection platform designed for air-gapped and restricted environments.

Key areas:
- Zero-dependency Go binary
- Real-time log ingestion
- Historical forensic analysis
- Linux syslog analysis
- Nginx access logs
- Docker logs
- Kubernetes logs
- Windows Event Log JSON
- Z-score anomaly detection
- Markov-chain behavioral analysis
- Threat detection and incident analysis

The project has been benchmarked at sub-200 ms analysis latency across its documented log sources and includes an evaluation showing approximately 38% fewer false-positive alerts when combining behavioral analysis with statistical detection versus the statistical baseline.

Status: In progress.

Technologies: Go, log analytics, anomaly detection, Markov chains, statistics, Linux, Windows, Docker, Kubernetes.

### SortMail

[Project](https://sortmail.rounakneema.in)

AI operating layer for professional email designed to work with Gmail and Outlook.

Key capabilities:
- Executive email briefings
- Email summarization
- Attachment intelligence
- Smart replies
- Task and priority extraction
- Follow-up detection
- Deadline extraction
- Calendar-oriented workflows
- AI-powered email search and reasoning

Security architecture includes OAuth security, authentication, authorization, rate limiting, attachment validation, malware/ZIP-bomb protections, secure secret management, monitoring, and privacy/compliance considerations.

Technologies: AI/LLMs, Gmail/Outlook integrations, APIs, OAuth, backend systems, databases, cloud infrastructure.

### SPQR

[Project](https://spqr.rounakneema.in)

Open-source contribution to SPQR, a distributed PostgreSQL sharding router.

Contribution:
- Implemented native Request Per Second (RPS) tracking in the Go routing layer.
- Added routing-layer performance instrumentation.
- Improved throughput observability and diagnosis of routing bottlenecks.
- Worked through GitHub pull requests, debugging, and code review.

Technologies: Go, PostgreSQL, distributed systems, database sharding, observability.

### PipelineForge

[Project](https://pipelineforge.rounakneema.in)

GitOps-based DevSecOps CI/CD deployment automation platform.

Key areas:
- GitHub Actions
- Docker image builds
- Trivy container vulnerability scanning
- Kubernetes deployments
- Helm
- Dev/staging environment promotion
- Automated rollback
- Kubernetes HPA
- NetworkPolicies
- Resource quotas
- k6 load testing
- Audit trails

A documented optimization reduced a Go Docker image from approximately 1.1 GB to approximately 8 MB using multi-stage and distroless builds, a reduction of approximately 99.3%.

Technologies: GitHub Actions, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Trivy, k6, GitOps, DevSecOps.

### DevContext.AI / Klarity

[Project](https://devcontext.rounakneema.in)

AI-powered repository intelligence platform that analyzes software repositories and converts them into engineering and interview intelligence.

Core capabilities:
- Repository analysis
- Code-quality analysis
- Architecture reconstruction
- Employability-oriented project analysis
- Evidence-grounded AI analysis
- Resume bullet generation
- Project-specific interview questions
- AI mock interviews
- Answer evaluation
- Follow-up questioning

Architecture includes a React frontend, AWS serverless backend, Amazon Bedrock, Claude models, repository processing, grounding validation, token-budget management, and asynchronous analysis pipelines.

Status: Active development.

Technologies: React, TypeScript, AWS, AWS Lambda/serverless, Amazon Bedrock, Claude, GitHub, LLMs.

### AXIOM OS

[Project](https://axiom-os.rounakneema.in)

Local-first personal operating system and AI accountability layer designed around behavioral telemetry, goal tracking, local memory, and contextual intervention.

Core architecture:
- Go telemetry daemon ("Specter")
- Local SQLite memory
- YAML-based goal definitions
- Local Ollama inference
- Behavioral event processing
- Context classification
- Goal alignment
- Policy-driven interventions
- Accountability and productivity workflows

The architecture is designed to minimize dependence on cloud AI and keep personal behavioral data local.

Status: In development.

Technologies: Go, Python, Java, SQLite, Ollama, local LLMs, browser integration, behavioral analytics.

### Dizzy

[Project](https://dizzy.rounakneema.in)

Voice-to-Figma generative UI system exploring natural-language design creation and modification through Figma MCP.

Conceptual workflow:

Voice → speech/agent reasoning → design intent → structured design operations → Figma MCP → native Figma design.

Key areas:
- Voice-driven UI generation
- Natural-language design commands
- Incremental design modification
- Design-state management
- Figma MCP
- Agentic UI generation

Status: In development.

Technologies: voice AI, LLM agents, Figma MCP, generative UI, structured design operations.
